BiblicalUsage: The Abanah is named once, in 2 Kings 5:12, when Naaman the leper objects to Elisha's command: 'Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean?' It is one of the two rivers of Damascus, clear and cold from Mount Hermon.
TheologicalSignificance: Naaman's question is still mine whenever God's way looks too plain: why this river, why this simple command, when I know better ones? I believe the Abanah teaches me that healing is not in the water I choose but in obeying the word God speaks — and Naaman had to go down into the Jordan to find that out.
